notes: These self-contained evals compare mode-specific design, deployment commands, diagnosis, and verification guidance against the recipe references. Guidance-only cases assume the stated inputs exist and must not access example /work or /models paths, start containers, download models, or execute REST calls. Expected files and settings can be shown as proposed content in the response. Clarification cases must pause on missing inputs instead of fabricating artifacts. Verification cases grade the proposed checks and evidence requirements, not claims of a live deployment. Do not copy Metro's fixed seven-container topology or Grafana 11.5.4 pin into this recipe's different architecture.

Assume the checkout contains docker-compose.yml, Makefile, and apps/, and /data/pump.csv contains vibration_mm_s. Use a rule-based UDF that flags vibration_mm_s > 12, OPC-UA simulator ingestion, MQTT alerts on alerts/pump-vibration, dashboard title Pump Vibration, and generated tests. Keep the existing default app. Guidance only: do not access these example paths, write files, start services, download anything, or execute REST calls.
evals.expected_output: A proposed apps/pump-vibration-monitor/ scaffold, registration preserving the default, an OPC-UA adapter for the non-wind-turbine schema, streaming UDF packaging/configuration, MQTT-only alerts, Grafana dashboard, tests, and the correct Makefile deployment procedure.
expectations: Selects ts production mode and places the app under apps/pump-vibration-monitor/ in the specified existing checkout
Appends pump-vibration-monitor to SAMPLE_APP_LIST without changing DEFAULT_SAMPLE_APP and reuses the shared topology rather than generating a new app-local docker-compose.yml
Uses the streaming UDF pattern and does not generate unsupported batch-mode config files

Explains that the bundled OPC-UA simulator is hardcoded to wind-turbine fields and proposes a per-app CSV/node adapter for vibration_mm_s with matching Telegraf nodes, rather than assuming any CSV works
Enables exactly one alert channel, MQTT, and uses alerts/pump-vibration as the alert topic
The proposed UDF reads vibration_mm_s and flags values strictly greater than 12, not equal to 12
Generates tests because the user explicitly requested them
Keeps config.json at or below 5 KB and omits a models key for the rule-based threshold UDF

Names the package apps/pump-vibration-monitor/time-series-analytics-config/pump-vibration-monitor.tar after the app and uses make up_opcua_ingestion app=pump-vibration-monitor to upload it before applying config
Obeys the guidance-only request and does not claim the app was deployed or tests passed

evals.prompt: Describe the proposed multimodal stack in /work/stacks/weld-quality-stack. Assume the user-supplied vision IR /models/weld.xml with its companion .bin and paired sample video /data/weld.avi and CSV /data/weld.csv already exist. Dashboard slug weld-quality; generate tests. Cover: the exact vision-pipeline element properties that provide the timestamp Fusion matches on and the startup warm-up; which topic each service publishes and subscribes to; how vision and sensor messages are paired; an example fused-verdict JSON payload; and the InfluxDB measurement(s) used for raw vision metadata and for fused verdicts. Guidance only: do not access these example paths, write files, start services, download anything, or execute REST calls.
evals.expected_output: A proposed flat multimodal stack with separate raw, processed, and anomaly-only topics, complete timestamp-aware vision/sensor fusion, stored raw vision and fused data, and tests. No deployment is performed.
expectations: Builds the multimodal shape as a new flat stack directory at the requested location, not an apps/<name>/ folder
Configures Fusion Analytics with FUSION_MODE=AND and TOLERANCE_NS=50e6
Keeps weld/sensor/raw and weld/sensor/processed as distinct topics and subscribes Fusion to the processed topic rather than the raw topic
Publishes every processed sensor point to weld/sensor/processed and only anomalies to weld/sensor/alerts so normal observations remain available for fusion

Enables RTP reference timestamps on the vision pipeline (add-reference-timestamp-meta=true and add-rtp-timestamp=true) so Fusion matches on the RTP sender NTP timestamp, and allows the initial roughly 300-packet warm-up
Pairs sensor and vision messages by timestamps within tolerance instead of fusing only the latest messages
Publishes the fused verdict on weld/fused-alerts as a flat JSON object (no nested objects) with fused_decision as a top-level scalar, e.g. shown in the example payload
Persists raw vision metadata for every frame, independently of matching, to its own named InfluxDB measurement that is separate from the fused-verdict measurement

evals.prompt: Explain the recipe's fusion result for these cases, without running code or services. Tolerance is 50 ms. Case A: one anomalous sensor observation has no matching camera observation. Case B: anomalous camera and sensor observations are 49 ms apart. Case C: anomalous camera and sensor observations are 51 ms apart. Compare AND and OR, describe missing-timestamp payload fields, and explain how timestamps are parsed and paired.
evals.expected_output: Correct first-come-first-served nearest-timestamp pairing and unmatched OR behavior; AND requires a match and both flags, OR preserves a lone anomaly, and missing source timestamps/delta are null rather than fabricated.
expectations: Case A yields no anomalous AND verdict but does publish and persist an anomalous OR verdict with the missing modality's flag recorded as 0
Case B is within tolerance and combines both anomaly flags, yielding an anomalous verdict for AND and OR
Case C cannot be treated as a matched pair for AND, while OR can still emit an unmatched source anomaly rather than suppressing it solely because no match exists
For unmatched OR verdicts sets the missing timestamp and delta_ms to JSON null and omits unavailable fields from the InfluxDB point
Reads the vision RTP sender timestamp and defensively parses sensor timestamps with fractional seconds up to 9 digits and optional timezone suffixes into epoch nanoseconds
